# Ray Sampling and Generation

Also called: Primary Ray Generation, Ray Bundle Construction

## Overview
Ray Sampling and Generation constructs the geometric primitives (origins $\mathbf{o}$ and directions $\mathbf{d}$) required for volume rendering, mapping 2D pixel coordinates to 3D world-space rays . It solves the initialization problem for volumetric integration by providing structured sampling points along the viewing frustum . It differs from its siblings by focusing on the geometric transformation from pixel indices to ray vectors, whereas methods like [Near-Far Linear Ray Generation](6841-near-far-linear-ray-generation.md) focus on depth discretization along those rays, and [Refined Ray Generation via PDF Sampling](6837-refined-ray-generation-via-pdf-sampling.md) focuses on adaptive depth sampling based on prior weights .

## Shared principles
The shared principles of this family are the geometric definition of rays and the parallel execution model [G].

**Ray Definition**
Rays are defined by an origin $\mathbf{o}$ and a direction $\mathbf{d}$ [G]. The direction is typically normalized. The origin is often the camera eye position, but can vary based on the camera model [G].

**Parallel Execution**
Computations are mapped to parallel threads [G]. Each thread typically processes one or more pixels or samples [G]. Memory access patterns are optimized for coalescing [G]. Synchronization is used to manage data dependencies between threads [G].

## Subtopics

### [Grid Ray Sampler](3930-grid-ray-sampler.md)
The [Grid Ray Sampler](#3930-grid-ray-sampler.md) generates a set of 3D camera rays by mapping pixel coordinates from an image grid to world space using camera intrinsics and extrinsics. It solves the problem of initializing the ray origins and directions required for volume rendering or [neural radiance field (NeRF) training](#970-nerf-training-loop.md) by providing a structured set of sampling points along the viewing frustum. It differs from its siblings by focusing on the geometric transformation from 2D pixel indices to 3D ray vectors, whereas methods like [Near-Far Linear Ray Generation](6841-near-far-linear-ray-generation.md) focus on depth discretization along those rays, and [Refined Ray Generation via PDF Sampling](6837-refined-ray-generation-via-pdf-sampling.md) focuses on adaptive depth sampling based on prior weights. Choose this method when a full or random subset of the image grid is required for [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) training or standard perspective rendering.

### [Camera Ray Generation](7456-camera-ray-generation.md)
[Camera Ray Generation](#7456-camera-ray-generation.md) computes the 3D origin $\mathbf{o}$ and direction $\mathbf{d}$ for primary rays corresponding to each pixel in an image, mapping 2D raster coordinates to 3D world-space rays for volume rendering or ray tracing. It differs from [Orthographic (Parallel) Camera Ray Generation](1319-orthographic-parallel-camera-ray-generation.md) by supporting perspective projection (converging rays) and from [Pinhole Camera Ray Generation](5058-pinhole-camera-ray-generation.md) by explicitly constructing and utilizing camera parameters (intrinsic/extrinsic or basis vectors) rather than assuming a canonical pinhole model [G]. It serves as the foundational step for [Ray Casting](6080-ray-casting.md) and [Ray Marching](3487-compute-shader-ray-marching-setup.md) [G]. Choose this method when explicit control over viewport bounds, basis vectors, or inverse view matrices is required.

### [Ray Sample Generation](12271-ray-sample-generation.md)
[Ray Sample Generation](#12271-ray-sample-generation.md) constructs `RaySamples` from a `RayBundle` and bin boundaries, projecting points along ray directions to create [frustums for volume](#2758-froxel-volume-frustum-grid.md) rendering. It serves as the bridge between camera geometry and volumetric integration, defining the spatial extent and sampling intervals for each ray. Unlike sibling methods that define ray origins or directions (e.g., [Camera Ray Generation](7456-camera-ray-generation.md)), this method focuses on the discretization of the ray path into manageable segments (frustums) with associated geometric properties. Choose this method when preparing inputs for volumetric integration that requires explicit frustum geometry and delta distances.

## Background
The geometric definition of rays originates from classical ray tracing [G]. The specific application to [Neural Radiance Fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) (NeRF) popularized the grid-based sampling of rays from intrinsic/extrinsic matrices for training . The construction of `RaySamples` with frustum geometry is a later development in [differentiable volumetric rendering](#775-differentiable-volumetric-rendering-dvr.md) to enable accurate density and color integration .
